scenes.say: Ever mess up a commit in Git? How do you actually fix it without losing work?

scenes.label: Reset
scenes.sub: Moves HEAD, can change files or index
scenes.say: Reset moves the head pointer, and can also change your files or staging area.
Revert makes a new commit to undo changes, which is safe for shared history. Restore recovers files or even branches, but leaves commit history alone.

scenes.title: Reflog in action
lines: a1b2c3d HEAD@{1}: reset: moving to HEAD~1
scenes.say: Reflog tracks every move of the head. Use it to find lost commits and bring them back.

scenes.question: What's safer for shared history?
scenes.right: git revert creates a safe undo commit
scenes.say: Here's a trap: Which is safer for shared history? It's revert, since it creates a new commit instead of erasing history.
